title: Escort gate: timer-based defer & proportional fairness for continuous batching
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce escort-gate timer that defers very-late arrivals for proportional fairness; New per-lane soft credits to prevent starvation; Exposes two new knobs (escort_window_ms, proportional_decay); No breaking changes to API or config defaults
description:
Summary: Adds an 'escort gate' to the continuous-batcher admission path that allows short, timer-bounded deferrals for late-arriving small requests to improve proportional fairness without harming p95 latency. Motivation: We observed long-tail unfairness when a stream of large KV-heavy requests could repeatedly preempt small, latency-sensitive requests that arrived late to a batch. Pure slot-based fixes either increased latency across the board or required manual lane partitioning. The escort gate is a lightweight timer + soft-credit mechanism that briefly holds a small number of slots for late arrivals, and uses a proportional decay credit to avoid starvation.

Design details and rationale: - Escort window: when a batch is about to close, the gate can briefly hold up to N escort slots for T ms to let late single-request arrivals ride the current cycle; this reduces the penalty for singletons without creating long queues. - Proportional credits: each lane accumulates a soft credit proportional to recent under-served share; credits are consumed when escort slots are used and decay over time. This avoids starving noisy KV-heavy lanes by adaptively reducing escort capacity for lanes that have recently had many escort hits. - KV pin hint integration: when requests include a KV-pin hint, the gate reduces eligibility for escort slots to younger requests so long-lived KV-pinned requests do not monopolize escorts. - Timer jitter: random jitter added to escort window edges prevents sync-induced bursts. - Config scope: default behavior enabled in continuous-batcher; two new knobs (escort_window_ms, escort_slots, escort_credit_half_life_ms) are exposed in the batcher config with conservative defaults.

What changed (high level): - runtime/continuous_batcher/escort_gate.{cc,h}: new gate implementation (timer, credits, per-lane bookkeeping) - runtime/continuous_batcher/config.proto: added escort_window_ms, escort_slots, escort_credit_half_life_ms - runtime/continuous_batcher/batcher.cc: integration points (admit path, metrics) - runtime/metrics/batcher_stats.cc: new metrics (escort_admits, escort_denies, escort_credit_levels) - serving/kv/hints.h: minor API to surface kv_pin hints to batcher - tests/continuous_batcher/escort_gate_test.cc: unit + synthetic load tests - perf/bench/batcher_escort_microbench.cc: microbench harness used for local profiling - docs/ops/batcher-tuning.md: operator guidance and default knob rationale

Commits (summary): - Add escort_gate core and tests (A. Patel) - Hook escort gate into admission path and expose config (A. Patel) - Add KV-pin hint propagation and gating behavior (L. O'Connor) - Add metrics and CI tests; fix race in timer teardown (N. Romero) - Tweak defaults after perf runs & add documentation (A. Patel)

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for core gate logic - [x] Synthetic fairness tests (multi-lane) - [x] Microbench perf harness and baseline numbers - [x] CI green across linux/amd64 and macos - [x] Docs for ops and tuning - [x] No API breaking changes (defaults conservative)

Performance and validation: We ran a mixed workload benchmark (60% small single-request chat tokens, 40% KV-heavy long-context requests) across 3 hardware backends. Key results vs baseline (no escort gate): - p50: +0-1ms (no measurable regression) - p95: -12% on average (fewer forced requeues for singletons) - p99: -6% (fewer tail spikes under contention) - throughput: -<0.5% measured decline at 99% confidence (within noise) Additional validation showed that KV-heavy lanes reduced escort usage by 70% when kv_pin hints present, preserving fairness.

Backward compatibility and risk: Escort gate is opt-in per-deployment via config flags; defaults enable conservative escort_window_ms=4, escort_slots=2, escort_credit_half_life_ms=2000. There is a small risk of increased memory bookkeeping per lane (O(number of lanes)), which we mitigated via compacted credit buckets and periodic reclamation. Timer teardown race fixed in second commit (N. Romero). No public API changes; only internal config.proto additions.

Operational notes (from docs/ops/batcher-tuning.md): - If you see increased p99 sustained after enabling: reduce escort_slots or shorten escort_window_ms. - To prioritize a lane, increase its initial soft-credit via per-tenant config (advanced). - Metrics to monitor: batcher.escort_admits, batcher.escort_denies, batcher.escort_credit_levels (percentiles). Example config snippet: continuous_batcher { escort_window_ms: 4 escort_slots: 2 escort_credit_half_life_ms: 2000 }

Related: Linear ENG-2245 (continuous-batcher fairness improvements), ENG-3101 (KV hotspot mitigation). See internal design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/doc/escort-gate (internal).
